companion_apps.name: TEPRA Lite
companion_apps.notes: Vendor app reviewed at Android version 2.6.2 (334); no account is needed by the direct community clients.

identity.notes: Address stability across units and firmware was not investigated; no serial-number identity is declared.

methods.notes: Match either name prefix, then confirm the FFF0/FFF1/FFF2 GATT layout after connecting. Do not extend the print sequence to an LR30SG or LR5 on name evidence alone.

host_compatibility.basis: The pinned tepra-lite-bleak README reports that stock Linux bluetoothd/BlueZ hides the FFF1 descriptor, so its ordinary Bleak backend cannot enable notifications. Its authors report success using a Bumble host stack over an HCI controller instead. Not reproduced by this project.
host_compatibility.notes: This is a host-stack descriptor-visibility problem, not evidence of pairing or authentication. A client that owns its ATT/host path over HCI can enable FFF1 notifications; use the cited Bumble/HCI route. Do not treat Write Without Response success as a working print path: replies and flow control still require FFF1.

host_compatibility.basis: The pinned direct client README reports its ordinary Bleak path working on Windows 10 and 11, and the public capture was made from a Windows host. Not reproduced by this project.

identification.notes: Both direct clients accept local names beginning LR30 or TepraBLE, including LR30, LR30 #1 and TepraBLE Demo. No advertised service UUID is asserted here: the sources establish FFF0 after connection, not that it appears in every advertisement. LR30SG can match the LR30 prefix but is not a verified variant.

device.name: KING JIM TEPRA Lite LR30
device.notes:
Phone-direct or computer-direct BLE label printer. The print path needs no Wi-Fi, vendor account, cloud session, PIN, or application-layer key. The optional ESP32 project is a user-hosted convenience bridge, not a printer dependency.
SCOPE. LR30 only. The vendor app also accepts the name LR30SG, but no LR30SG wire capture or client result establishes compatibility; an LR30 prefix match is therefore only a discovery candidate, not a compatibility claim. LR5 is excluded. No firmware-update mechanism, firmware image, or bootloader entry is established, so no update feature is declared.
TRANSPORT. Custom service 0000fff0-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb carries notifications on 0000fff1-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb and Write Without Response commands on 0000fff2-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb. Subscribe to FFF1 before the first FFF2 write. Host writes begin F0 and replies begin F1. The recovered message layer has no checksum or length envelope.
PRINTING. Render a 64-pixel-high monochrome canvas, pad its feed-direction width to at least 84 pixels and an even number, rotate clockwise 90 degrees, and pack each rotated row into eight bytes. Each F0 5C write carries two reordered rows: 16 raster bytes in an 18-byte GATT write. After every six data writes, wait for F1 5C. End with F0 5D 00, then poll F0 5E until F1 5E reports that the printer is no longer busy. The older written note says F1 5D for the poll reply, but its own public capture consistently carries F1 5E; this spec follows the capture.

openness.notes: No vendor protocol document was found. This spec derives the LR30 control surface from two independent open clients, static analysis of the vendor app, and the public capture linked under evidence.

enter_pairing_mode.notes: No pairing mode, button gesture, PIN, or bonding exchange is used by either direct client; the public capture contains no SMP exchange.

exclusivity.recovery: If another central holds the connection, close that client or power-cycle the printer, then reconnect; simultaneous-central behavior was not established.

pairing.notes: Basis: both open clients use an unpaired GATT connection and no PIN or application authentication, and the reviewed public capture has no SMP packets. This project did not test whether a host-initiated optional bond is accepted, so clients should not request one.

unpair.clears: Nothing: the documented flow creates no bond or per-client authorization record.
unpair.notes: Disconnecting is sufficient. There is no device-side bond to revoke, and no factory reset is required to adopt another host.

credentials.notes: BLE-only direct control with no application-layer credential or vendor account.

factory_reset.description: Do not infer a button sequence from another TEPRA model. The open clients and public capture establish no reset command or gesture.
factory_reset.effect: No factory-reset procedure or settings-clearing effect is established. No bond, network credential, account binding, or owner secret is created by the documented direct flow, so changing hosts requires no reset. A power cycle only ends the current connection; it is not claimed to restore factory settings.

methods.description: Power the LR30, select an LR30- or TepraBLE-prefixed advertisement, connect without pairing, and subscribe to FFF1 before printing.
methods.name: Direct BLE connection, no account or bond

steps.expect: An advertisement whose local name begins LR30 or TepraBLE.

steps.action: Scan for either documented name prefix and connect to the LR30.
steps.expect: A BLE GATT connection with FFF0, FFF1 and FFF2 present.

steps.action: Discover services and subscribe to notifications on 0000fff1-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb.
steps.expect: FFF1 notifications are enabled before any FFF2 command write.
steps.notes: On stock BlueZ this subscription can fail because the FFF1 descriptor is hidden; see device.host_compatibility.

steps.action: Run the print sequence in protocol_details.job_sequence.
steps.expect: The final F1 5E reply has busy byte 00.

causes: The direct client documents that bluetoothd hides the FFF1 descriptor. Use the documented alternate Bumble/HCI host path or Windows; do not send blind FFF2 writes without the reply channel.
troubleshooting.symptom: FFF1 notification subscription is unavailable on Linux/BlueZ.

setup.notes: No provisioning or account setup. Two independent clients scan, connect, enable FFF1 notifications and print without pairing or credentials. Confidence is medium because those are public implementations and a public capture, not a flow replayed by this project.

rejoin.notes: There is no Wi-Fi network or persistent bond to rejoin. Disconnect the old central, then scan and connect from the new one. No reset is needed.

testing.notes: No LR30 was driven by this project. The pinned public capture repo/tepra-lite-esp32/doc/sniffed_packets.pcapng was decoded and checked against both open clients. It corroborates F0 5A/5B/5C/5D/5E, six data writes per batch acknowledgement, and F1 5E busy/completion replies. The capture is public third-party evidence, not a capture made by this project, so individual protocol facts stay `reported`.

entities.name: Battery Level
entities.notes: Uncalibrated: a public bridge reports a persistent 99 percent reading. Display the raw value with this caveat rather than deriving charge health or runtime.

artifacts.description: Direct CPython/Bleak LR30 client: discovery, FFF1 subscription, F0 operations, depth mapping, pair permutation, six-write pacing and busy loop; its companion renderer establishes the 64-pixel canvas, width padding, clockwise rotation and row packing. Its README is the BlueZ caveat and Windows compatibility source.

Independent MicroPython LR30 client with the same GATT and print sequence, standard Battery Level read, written protocol note and public capture. Its REST bridge is user-hosted and is not presented as a printer requirement. Its client README supplies the uncalibrated 99 percent battery report.

Public LR30 BLE capture reviewed locally. It contains F0 5A/5B/5C/5D/5E, F1 5A/5B/5C/5D replies, and repeated F1 5E 01 00 polls ending in F1 5E 00 00. It also shows a final partial raster group followed directly by F0 5D 00. No owner address or unit-specific identifier is copied into this spec.

Corroborates the FFF0/FFF1/FFF2 roles, operation opcodes, depth range and name aliases. Vendor implementation symbols are deliberately not reproduced. Static analysis remains reported evidence, not hardware verification.

evidence.capture_review: The capture was read as ATT values, not inferred solely from the written reverse-engineering note. That distinction matters for poll_print_status: the note writes F1 5D 01 00 / F1 5D 00 00, while every corresponding captured notification is F1 5E 01 00 / F1 5E 00 00. The command and reply tables use F1 5E. No capture bytes are used to assign meanings to the four variable F1 5C bytes or the last F1 5E byte.
open_questions: An owner GATT/CCCD dump and a fresh print/status capture are still needed on current firmware.
LR30SG requires its own capture and client replay before becoming a variant; LR5 needs separate research.
Battery readings need comparison with known charge states before the raw percentage can be called calibrated.
The variable F1 5C payload, F1 5A/F1 5B fields, non-busy F1 5E values and the final F1 5E byte need status captures.

initialization.description: Enable printer-to-client notifications before any command or raster write.
initialization.notes: Required for prepare/depth replies, six-write flow control, end acknowledgement and busy polling.

covers: Batch flow control and busy/completion polling
Raw standard Battery Level reads, explicitly uncalibrated on LR30
not_covered: Firmware update: no update surface is established or declared
LR30SG and LR5: no wire compatibility is claimed
local_access.notes: A user-hosted ESP32 REST bridge exists but is optional and is not the protocol documented here.
local_access.summary: Direct local BLE printing from a phone or computer, with no vendor cloud, account, bridge or credentials in the required path.

job_sequence.description: One direct BLE print job. Subscribe to FFF1 on connection before entering this sequence. All command writes go to FFF2 without response; all waits read FFF1 notifications. Timeouts and the 20 ms data-write pause are the open clients' pacing choices, not established firmware minima.

steps.note: No separate batch wait after a final partial group of one through five writes.

print_depth.description: Signed depth d in -3..3 maps to one sign/magnitude byte. For d >= 0 the byte is d. For d < 0 it is 0x10 + abs(d), equivalently 0x10 - d. This is not two's complement: -3 is 13, not FD. Byte 3 of the command is always 06; its purpose is not established.

raster_encoding.canvas_width_rule: width = max(84, source_width); if width is odd, add 1
raster_encoding.description: Build an upright monochrome image whose height is 64 pixels (across the print head) and whose width is the feed direction. One means black and zero means white. The following transformation is exactly the open renderer's rotate-and-pack operation; the equivalent direct formula avoids requiring an imaging library.

padding.horizontal_placement: left = padded_width // 2 - source_width // 2; paste the full 64-pixel-high source there

rotation.row_order: Rotated rows top to bottom correspond to source columns left to right.

row_packing.algorithm: For each rotated row, visit rotated x coordinates 63 down to 0. For shift s = 0..63, set bit 1 << s when the visited pixel is black. Serialize the resulting unsigned 64-bit integer big-endian. Directly from the upright source, column x becomes one row: source pixel (x, y) maps to output byte 7 - (y // 8), bit y % 8. Thus byte 0 covers source y = 56..63 and byte 7 covers y = 0..7; within each byte the lower source y has the lower bit number.
row_packing.encoded_length_rule: padded_width * 8 bytes; even width makes this a multiple of 16

wire_pair_permutation.source_block: A0 A1 A2 A3 A4 A5 A6 A7 B0 B1 B2 B3 B4 B5 B6 B7 (two consecutive encoded rows)
wire_pair_permutation.wire_block: A6 A7 A4 A5 A2 A3 A0 A1 B6 B7 B4 B5 B2 B3 B0 B1
wire_pair_permutation.write: F0 5C followed by the 16-byte wire block, 18 bytes total

reply_frames.description: Multiplexed FFF1 notifications. Prefix and total length are stated so a client does not confuse the three-byte end acknowledgement with the four-byte poll reply. Unlisted payload semantics remain unknown.

fields.name: unknown
fields.observed: 00 in the public capture; no meaning assigned

poll_print_status.note: The repository's older written note calls these F1 5D; frames in its own capture are F1 5E. Follow the capture.

prepare.note: The ASCII TEPRA suffix is visible; other fields are not assigned meanings.

raster_batch.note: Wait after every six F0 5C writes. The four trailing bytes vary in the capture but their meaning is unknown; do not require one captured counter value.

set_print_depth.note: Observed after depth +1; no general status-byte semantics are claimed.

test_vectors.description: Synthetic vectors independently rebuilt by scripts/test_king_jim_tepra_lite.py using only the standard library for the algorithms. They are not presented as captured samples.

raster_pair.note: A two-column primitive isolates rotation and bit order; a real job first pads this canvas to 84 pixels.

remaining_unknowns: No hardware reset procedure, settings-clearing behavior, optional bonding behavior or simultaneous-central limit is established.
The maximum feed-direction image width, physical DPI, supported tape-media table and behavior above the clients' 84-pixel minimum are not established.
The exact threshold behavior of arbitrary non-1-bit image input is a renderer choice; the protocol here accepts an already monochrome canvas.
The meaning of F1 5C's four variable bytes, F1 5A/F1 5B non-prefix fields, F1 5E byte 3 and poll values other than 00/01 is unknown.
Battery Level is a raw SIG percentage whose LR30 calibration is unresolved; one public client reports that it stays at 99 percent.
Whether stock BlueZ versions that hide FFF1 can be fixed by configuration alone is unknown; the established reported workaround is an alternate Bumble/HCI host path or Windows.
LR30SG is an unverified app alias and LR5 is excluded. No firmware-update, bootloader, credential or vendor-cloud control surface is claimed.

format.name: battery_level
format.notes: SIG Battery Level percentage. The ESP32 bridge author reports that an LR30 returned 99 on every read, so this value is raw and uncalibrated, not a trustworthy estimate of remaining charge.

characteristics.name: Battery Level
characteristics.notes: Read-only access is established by the open bridge; notification support is not claimed.

services.name: Battery Service
services.notes: Standard Battery Service documented by the public LR30 protocol note. Only the percentage encoding of Battery Level is used; its calibration on this printer is not established.

characteristics.name: Printer Notifications
characteristics.notes: Replies begin F1. Prepare, depth, batch, end and poll replies share this characteristic, so correlate them with the outstanding command rather than treating every notification as a busy reply. Frame shapes are in protocol_details.reply_frames. Subscribe before using FFF2.

end_raster_data.description: F0 5D 00 — mark the end of raster data and wait for F1 5D 00 before polling.

poll_print_status.description: F0 5E — request print status; repeat while byte 2 of the four-byte F1 5E reply is 01 (busy). Capture: F1 5E 01 00 while busy and F1 5E 00 00 when complete. Treat other byte-2 values as unknown rather than declaring success. The older prose's F1 5D poll id is contradicted by its own capture.

prepare.description: F0 5A — begin or prepare a print job; wait for the F1 5A reply before setting depth. Captured reply: F1 5A 00 02 00 54 45 50 52 41 (the final five bytes are ASCII TEPRA). The meaning of the earlier fields is not fully mapped.

set_print_depth.description: F0 5B <depth> 06 — set print depth from -3 through +3 using the raw sign/magnitude byte, then wait for F1 5B. The trailing 06 is required by both clients; its meaning is unknown. Captured depth +1 answers F1 5B 00 06. Do not generalize the last two reply bytes into a status model.

depth.description: Raw sign/magnitude depth code, not an int8. Positive values 0..3 encode as 0x00..0x03; negative values -1..-3 encode as 0x10 plus the magnitude (0x11..0x13). The labels expose the signed setting while the allowed values emit the right byte.

write_raster_pair.description: F0 5C <16 bytes> — send two encoded raster rows after the pair permutation in protocol_details.raster_encoding. Send six such writes, then wait for a six-byte F1 5C notification. A trailing group of one through five writes is followed by end_raster_data without a separate batch wait, matching the open clients and capture.

raster_pair.description: Sixteen wire-order raster bytes: source indexes 6,7,4,5,2,3,0,1,14,15,12,13,10,11,8,9 of the next two eight-byte rows.

characteristics.name: Printer Commands
characteristics.notes: All five F0 operations are declared below. F0 5C carries exactly 16 raster bytes after F0 5C, making an 18-byte write. The public capture observes each operation; `observed: true` refers to that third-party capture and does not raise verification above `reported`.

services.name: TEPRA Lite Print Service
services.notes: LR30-specific command channel. FFF1 notifies and FFF2 accepts Write Without Response. Every operation is one GATT write, at most 18 bytes; there is no additional fragmentation, length prefix, checksum, encryption or pairing handshake in the recovered message layer.
